details:
ASTRAEON (Adaptive Space-Time Resilience & Autonomous Emergency Operations Network) is an intelligent astronaut health monitoring and mission-support system designed to improve safety during long-duration Moon and Mars missions.

Astronauts face challenges such as radiation exposure, microgravity, isolation, health changes, and habitat environmental risks. Communication delays with Earth can also make immediate assistance difficult. ASTRAEON addresses these challenges by connecting astronaut health, habitat conditions, mission status, crew capabilities, medical resources, and Earth communication in one integrated platform.

Its core innovation, the Adaptive Medical State Graph, connects these six dimensions to provide a broader understanding of mission conditions and support context-aware decision-making.

Key features include a Command Center, Crew Health Monitoring, Habitat Systems Monitoring, Early Warning and Alerts, an AI Mission Copilot, Crew and Medical Resource Management, Earth Communication Monitoring, Mission Map, Mission Timeline, and an interactive Emergency Scenario Simulator. The simulator demonstrates situations such as unusual heart-rate readings, elevated carbon dioxide, communication blackouts, and combined emergencies.

ASTRAEON helps organise mission information, highlight potential risks, track available resources, and support structured emergency responses. Its goal is to contribute to safer and more resilient human space exploration, especially when communication with Earth is limited.

The prototype was developed using React, Vite, JavaScript, Node.js, Express, Google Gemini AI, Firebase, and Leaflet. It currently uses simulated sensor readings and interactive controls to demonstrate its workflow; real astronaut sensor integration is a future development goal.

What makes ASTRAEON creative is its integrated approach: rather than monitoring health, environment, crew, and resources separately, it connects them to understand how changes in one area can affect the entire mission. Future development could include wearable sensors, NASA open datasets, personalised health profiles, and advanced offline decision-support capabilities.

ASTRAEON — Connecting astronaut health, mission intelligence, and adaptive decision support for the future of space exploration.
